On 15 November 1988 the Soviet space shuttle Buran, "snowstorm", took off from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan, circled the Earth twice and landed itself on a runway, with no crew aboard. It was the first fully automatic landing of a spaceplane, and the only flight Buran ever made.

The Soviets began the programme in the 1970s in answer to the American Space Shuttle, which they feared could serve as a weapon. Buran looked much like it, but it was carried up by the separate Energia rocket, the most powerful of its day, and had no main engines of its own.

The collapse of the Soviet Union ended it; Russia cancelled the programme in 1993. In 2002 the roof of its hangar at Baikonur fell in, destroying the orbiter and killing eight workers. Other unfinished orbiters still stand at the site. The flight came thirty one years after Sputnik 1 was launched from the same cosmodrome.
